recentItems.title: Leaders of South Korea and Uzbekistan meet for summit in Seoul
recentItems.description:
(14 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Seoul, South Korea - 14 September 2026
1. Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev walking with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung ahead of welcome ceremony
2. Various of Mirziyoyev and Lee during welcome ceremony 
3. Mid of officials during welcome ceremony 
4. Various of Mirziyoyev and Lee walking, reviewing troops
5. Various of Mirziyoyev and Lee greeting guests, some waving flags 
6. Mirziyoyev and Lee shaking hands and psoing for photos
7. Various of meeting between Mirziyoyev, Lee and delegations 
STORYLINE:
Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung for talks on Monday during his trip to Seoul.

Mirziyoyev was welcomed with an honor guard ceremony, which was followed by talks in South Korea's presidential office. 

Mirziyoyev, who arrived in Seoul on Sunday, is on a state visit for the inaugural Korea-Central Asia Summit, which is scheduled to take place on September 16. 

South Korea is hosting the leaders of five Central Asian nations - Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan - during the summit. 

AP video shot by: Yong-ho Kim

recentItems.title: Daily China MOFA Briefing Highlights
recentItems.description:
(14 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS  
Beijing -  14 September 2026

MOFA Highlights                                      
Spokesperson: Guo Jiakun
Date: 14 September 2026
Duration:  04 min 08 sec

1. President Xi Jinping met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, at the weekend. The leaders of China and India have successfully met for three consecutive years. Does China have a comment on the China-India relations going forward? 

The two leaders have once again provided strategic guidance and direction for the development of China-India relations. China stands ready to work with India to fully implement the important consensus reached by the two leaders, continuously expand the list of areas of cooperation, strengthen people-to-people exchanges, and deepen multilateral coordination, so as to promote the sustained improvement and development of bilateral relations, support each other's development and revitalization, and jointly contribute to peace and prosperity in the region and beyond.

2.It is reported that Iran acquired satellite imagery from Chinese entities before it attacked a US base in Jordan in July, which killed three US troops. Does China have a response to this? 

As a responsible major power, China has been strictly fulfilling its international obligations. We firmly oppose unfounded suspicions and accusations made without evidence.

3.It is reported that Yemen's Houthis have attacked four cities in Saudi Arabia, injuring over 70 civilians and damaging multiple energy and civilian infrastructure. Does China have any comments? 

Recently, tensions have escalated in Yemen and the Red Sea, causing casualties among innocent civilians and damage to civilian infrastructure, including energy facilities. China is deeply concerned about this situation. 
Attacks on civilian infrastructure that is important to people’s livelihoods are unacceptable. Increased instability in the region is not in the interests of any party, and the sovereignty and security of all countries must be respected. 
Resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means is the only way out. China calls on all relevant parties to exercise restraint and ease tensions through communication and dialogue to promote de-escalation as soon as possible.

4.Dario Amodei, Sam Altman and Elon Musk all over the weekend called on AI companies to slow down frontier development. Amodei argued a Chinese advantage in AI would pose US national security risks. Does the Foreign Ministry have any comments?

The development of artificial intelligence is crucial to the well-being of all humanity, and all parties should work together to promote an open and inclusive development of AI for good and for all. Fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance which serves no one's interest.

5.Recently, some Panamanian lawmakers established a Panama-Taiwan interparliamentary cross-party exchange group with U.S. lawmakers participating in the meeting online. What is China’s comment?

The establishment of such a group seriously violates Panama’s long-standing commitment to the one-China principle. We have noted the relevant remarks by the Panamanian government. We hope Panama will put the one-China principle into practice and safeguard the political foundation of China-Panama relations. 


STORYLINE:

recentItems.title: Hindus in India welcome brightly decorated idols of Ganesha as Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations start
recentItems.description:
(14 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTIONS SUMMARY: 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Hyderabad, India – 14 September 2026
1. Tilt down of a 69-foot-tall Ganesh (elephant-headed Hindu god) idol in the Khairatabad neighborhood
2. Mid of devotees dancing to the beat of drums in front of the idol
3. Devotees offering prayers in front of the idol
4. Various of the idol surrounded by devotees
5. Mid of an artist putting the finishing touches on a Ganesha idol
6. Devotee holding a Ganesha idol inside a shop
7. People looking at Ganesha idols in a shop
8. Various of Ganesha idols on display
9. Various of outdoor flower market, people buying flowers for religious offerings

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Mumbai, India – 14 September 2026
10. Tracking shot of a Ganesha idol being transported on a truck accompanied by devotees
11. Various of devotees taking Ganesha idols home as drummers perform
12. Wide of devotees chanting as they accompany an idol being transported on a truck
13. Various of Ganesha idols on display in a shop
14. Various of devotees carrying Ganesha idols away
15. Mid of an idol
16. Various of people carrying idols away
STORYLINE:
Hindus across India began celebrating Ganesh Chaturthi on Monday, welcoming brightly decorated idols of Ganesha (elephant-headed Hindu god of wisdom and prosperity) into their homes and temporary public shrines.

In Mumbai and Hyderabad, families and community groups crowded markets to collect idols and buy flowers, sweets and other religious offerings.

From small statues being carried home by families to towering idols being transported on trucks, images of Ganesha filled the streets of both cities.

The festival celebrates the birth of Ganesha, who is revered as the remover of obstacles.

In Hyderabad, one of the main attractions is a 69-foot-tall, five-faced Ganesha idol installed in the Khairatabad neighborhood.

Devotees gathered around the towering idol to offer prayers, dance, and celebrate to the beat of drums.

In Mumbai, devotees carried idols to their homes and elaborately decorated community pandals, accompanied by drummers and chants of “Ganpati Bappa Morya(Hail our Lord Ganesha, honoring the great devotee Morya).”

The festivities conclude with colorful processions during which the idols are immersed in bodies of water.

AP video shot by Mahesh Kumar and Rafiq Maqbool

recentItems.title: International Energy Agency chief Birol meets Japan PM Takaichi in Tokyo
recentItems.description:
(14 Sep 2026) 
RESTIRCTION SUMMARY: 
++AUDO AS INCOMING++

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Tokyo, Japan -  14 September 2026
1. IEA (International Energy Agency) executive director Fatih Birol greets Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi
2. Various of Birol and Takaichi pose for photo
3. SOUNDBITE (English) Fatih Birol, IEA Executive Director:
“These two major initiatives, you have ‘POWER GX and POWER Asia’ are excellent initiatives, very timely, good for Japan, good for Asia Pacific, and good for the world. I am ready...(inaudible) to support you fully there, Madam Prime Minister .”
4. Takaichi speaking
5. SOUNDBITE (English) Fatih Birol, IEA Executive Director:
“It is the entire work is affected with this crisis (conflicts in the Middle East), and it seems it will take much longer than many people thought. The entire world is affected, but Asia is mostly affected. It is the reason why I recently attended the Asia Pacific energy minister's meeting. Today in Tokyo meeting, it’s an honor to meet you (Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi) and your ministers, the minister of foreign affairs and the minister... (inaudible).”
6. Pan from Takaichi to Birol
STORYLINE:
IEA (International Energy Agency) executive director Fatih Birol met with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi of Japan in Tokyo on Monday. 

He praised Japan’s leadership in energy security, as the war in the Middle East is acutely affecting energy supplies. 

“POWER GX and POWER Asia are excellent initiatives, very timely, good for Japan, good for Asia Pacific, good for the world. I am ready to support you fully,” Birol told Takaichi. 

Birol also met with the Japanese foreign minister and the minister of economy, trade and industry.

He will head to South Korea on Tuesday to meet the country’s President Lee Jae Myung.

AP video shot by Ayaka McGill

recentItems.title: Iraq's National Orchestra delighted audience with a special concert of classical music
recentItems.description:
(14 Sep 2026) 
IRAQ ORCHESTRA

SOURCE: ASSOCIATED PRESS

RESTRICTION SUMMARY: 

LENGTH: 3:00

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Baghdad, Iraq – 10 September 2026
1. Various of Iraq's National Symphony Orchestra performing on stage 
2. Various of conductor Mohammed Amin leading the orchestra 
3. Various of musicians performing in concert 
4. Various of people watching the concert 
5. Woman filming the show with her mobile phone 
6. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Mohammed Amin, conductor of Iraqi symphony orchestra:
“Bolero by (Maurice) Ravel is a very important work, and this was performed (for the first time) after more than 41 years. It was performed by the Iraqi national symphony in 1985 with orchestra conductor Akoka. I attended that concert, as a new graduate from Romania. It was a fabulous concert, and at that time, 80% of orchestra members were foreigners. Today, we are playing Bolero after 41 years with an Iraqi orchestra and conductor.”

7. Pan of audience and orchestra  
8. Various of Amin conducting the performance
9. Various of musicians playing their instruments 
10. Top shot of Iraq's National Symphony Orchestra
11. Various of audience outside the concert hall
12. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Luma Qais, attendee from Baghdad:
“This concert by the Iraqi national symphony is a very nice event and we wish for it happen again in the future. Listening to music is a remedy for soul and it is an international language, where a person can enjoy it anywhere, and music reaches the heart easily. It is a knowledge and a beautiful special world. These sorts of events should be held very often in Baghdad and in Iraq in general.”

13. Various of Iraqi National Theatre building in Baghdad
STORYLINE:
Iraq's national symphony regaled its audience with a performance that paid tribute to masters of classical music such as French composer Maurice Ravel and Italian composer Giuseppe Verdi. 

Founded in 1944 by Albert Chafoo, Iraq's orchestra is one of the oldest in the region. 

Conductor Mohammed Amin reminisced on his memory of hearing Ravel's famous Bolero in 1985 as a new graduate coming back from Romania. 

At the time, the orchestra mostly consisted of foreign musicians. Now, he said,  it’s composed by 90 Iraqi musicians coming from different ethnic and religious backgrounds.

"Today, we are playing Bolero after 41 years with an Iraqi orchestra and conductor," he said. 

Luma Qais, an attendee from Baghdad, lauded the performance. 

They mainly played western and soviet compositions, and to Qais, it represented how music remains "an international language."

"It is a remedy for the soul.. and music reaches the heart easily."

Although the national orchestra mainly performs locally, it has in the past toured in Lebanon, Jordan and France. 

AP video by Ali Jabar

recentItems.title: Palestinians build and repair homes with mud and wood while Gaza's reconstruction remains distant
recentItems.description:
(14 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Shati refugee camp, Gaza City, Gaza Strip - 2 September 2026 
1. Shati refugee camp resident, Alaa Jouda, climbing stairs to his wooden home built on top of rubble of his destroyed house

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Shati refugee camp, Gaza City, Gaza Strip - 10 September 2026 
2. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Alaa Jouda, resident of Shati refugee camp: ++SOUNDBITE STARTS ON PREVIOUS SHOT AND IS OVERLAID BY SHOT 3++
”The main reason of using wood was due to the lack of construction materials and supplies. While we used wood as a substitute for cement, it certainly does not replace our original cement homes.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Shati refugee camp, Gaza City, Gaza Strip - 2 September 2026 
3. Various of Jouda in his wooden home

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Maghazi, Central Gaza Strip - 3 September 2026 
4. Various of man filling molds with mud

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Maghazi, Central Gaza Strip - 5 September 2026 
5. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Khalil Abu Ramadan, displaced from northern Gaza: ++SOUNDBITE STARTS ON SHOT 4-5 AND IS OVERLAID BY SHOT 7++
”The idea of building a room out of mud came to me because we were living in tents that offered no protection against the winter cold or the summer heat. I researched on the internet how our ancestors used to build such structures and put that knowledge into practice.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Maghazi, Central Gaza Strip - 3 September 2026 
6. Various of man filling moulds with mud

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Maghazi, Central Gaza Strip - 5 September 2026 
7. Various of Abu Ramadan and his friends building house using mud mold bricks

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Gaza City, Gaza Strip - 7 September 2026 
8. Various of workers covering walls in shop using nylon and fabric
9. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Ismat Dader, resident from Gaza City: ++SOUNDBITE STARTS ON PREVIOUS SHOT AND IS OVERLAID BY SHOT 10-11++
”We managed to find solutions for the owner of a destroyed facility - which was his sole source of livelihood - transforming a pile of rubble and debris into something that allows him to restart his business and provide for his home and family, starting from nothing.”
10. Various of workers inside building
11. Various of workers covering walls with nylon 
STORYLINE:
Across Gaza residents have been using improvised materials and small-scale repairs to make damaged homes and businesses habitable again, even as a broader reconstruction effort has yet to begin. 

Aid agencies have warned that rebuilding the territory on a large scale could take years because of the vast destruction and restrictions on materials entering Gaza.

In the Shati refugee camp, Alaa Jouda has built a wooden home on top of the rubble of his destroyed house.

He said he created the building using materials he already had and by purchasing additional materials at a cost of about 25,000 shekels ($7,000).

“While we used wood as a substitute for cement, it certainly does not replace our original cement homes,” he said.

After months of displacement, Khalil Abu Ramadan has been building a home for his family using mud molds in central Gaza.

He said he was creating the building using an ancient construction method with access to conventional building materials severely restricted.

For Abu Ramadan, the alternative was mud. 

He had been living in tents after being displaced from northern Gaza to a refugee camp in Deir al-Balah.

“The idea of building a room out of mud came to me because we were living in tents that offered no protection against the winter cold or the summer heat," he said.











AP video produced by: Wafaa Shurafa
